title: Square of the Quadratic Gauss Sum

problemStatement.formal:
\text{For an odd prime } p \text{ and a primitive } p\text{-th root of unity } \zeta_p,\quad
g = \sum_{n=0}^{p-1} \left(\frac{n}{p}\right) \zeta_p^{\,n},\quad g^2 = (-1)^{(p-1)/2}\,p.
problemStatement.plain: Weight each residue $n$ by the Legendre symbol $(n/p)$ (which is $+1$ for squares, $-1$ for non-squares). The square of this Gauss sum equals $p^* = (-1)^{(p-1)/2} p$.
